results.title: Fusion of Serenity and Divinity @ Kathmandu
results.text:
One of the most important temples of Bhagwan Shiva situated at the banks of river Bagmati in Kathmandu.This temple is one of the seven UNESCO heritage sites in Nepal. A must visit temple for all Hindus.

Adjacent to the Bhairav temple, unique 525 Lingams are installed in a Swastika shaped maze. For good health and longevity, one has to do parikrama (cumambulate) walk through a maze like path touching all the lingams and then exit from a different end.Though the temple opens at 4 am and closes after evening aarti at 7.30 pm. During the day, temple is closed between 12 noon to 5 pm. Depending on the time available at your disposal, best would be to be there well before 7 pm to join the Arti and have Darshan of other temples in the compound. Om Namah Shivaya

results.title: Very shocking and eye-opening experience
results.text:
My boyfriend and I visited Pashupatinath Temple with open and intrigued minds and we learnt so much in the process. We paid for a guide and are pleased we did so as we would have cluelessly walked into the funerals otherwise. Be aware that the guides pounce on you and then charge 1000 rupees at the end - we were unaware of this cost and didn’t have enough to cover it! 
The area is impressive and very busy, with lots of temples to admire. The riverside is where the rituals take place and you can view from above. Having the guide meant we learnt about the rituals and understood what was happening. Very shocking for us westerners but an eye-opening experience.

results.title: Sacred Heritage
results.text: We visited Nepal primarily to take Darshan of Lord Pashupatinath with our family. We could take very nice darshan from all sides of temple. You would find many shrines inside the temple but two or most important. One is of Lord Pashupatinath and another temple of Lord Nagraj. No kind of mobiles or cameras allowed inside shrine !

results.title: Old Shiva Temple- A Must visit place for Hindus
results.text: Monday's are very crowded. If you are a first time visitor, please avoid. Other days you can see the temple peacefully; spend time in each diety. Worth a visit of 2 hrs.

results.title: One of my most favourite spot in Kathamandu
results.text: A very popular spot similar to the ghats of Vanarasi, but a smaller scale. I love this spot very much, sitting along the riverside, watching families saying goodbye to their beloved ones, a bit sad but very peaceful...

results.title: Hindu burial rites
results.text: Colorful and interesting glance into another culture.  A fascinating place to wander a bit.  Complete with yogis, monkeys and vagrant dogs. Having a guide made it much more intelligible to a benighted westerner.

results.title: Divinity is Ultimate
results.text: Visited the shrine in Sept. 2019. It was Sunday and so not crowded . Went from Thamel by taxi with fare Rs. 600/- On reaching walked on foot to the sanctum sanctorum.  Only a handful persons were there in Q. Had Darshan from the gate where the Priest took flowers from my had and offered to Lord. Highly satisfying. Then had parikrama and found other temples situated in the premises. There is a Unmat Bhairav Temple in one side which one must visit after Lord Pashupatinath Darshan. Also saw rituals on the bank of river Baghmati on which bank this famous Temple is situated. Namah Shivay.

results.title: Pashupatinath visit
results.text: The temple complex is huge and the whole place is beautiful, the nearby shops selling religious items add to the beauty and sanctity of the temple. Here Rudraksh is famous and one can see almost everyone wearing a rudraksh mala. The temple is pristine in its glory, the main temple has 4 deities of Lord Shiva carved into one single stone so one can view the beauty of the Lord from all 4 angles during the pradakshina. It is a known fact that the King of Nepal himself used to do the pooja of the lord. A must see on every visitor's itinerary visiting Nepal.

results.title: a must visit place
results.text:
So, here is why you should visit the temple and what you could expect.
1.	It is one of the four most important religious sites in Asia for Shiva devotees. 
2.	The largest temple complex in Nepal.
3.	this is UNESCO designated cultural heritage site.
4.	The streets around the temple can show the street selling culture of the country. They sell mostly worship items and other items related to Hindu traditions. 
5.	There are also enough places to eat for cheap if you feel hungry. 
6.	As a foreigner you can experience the Hindu cremation culture. 
7.	Monkeys are also present in large numbers and they are the kings there.
8.	People swimming in the river for holy bathing as well as looking for valuable 
9.	You can also meet sadhus (sages) who have an amazing appearance. You can also meet fortune tellers.
10.	At evening, if it does not rain, then you can also experience the “ aarati” which happens just beside the bagmati river and Infront of the Shiva temple.
11.	The temple is very old so you can also experience the ancient art and architecture of the country.

results.title: Divine
results.text: Energy of the place is amazing. Arrangements for Darshan was proper and cleanliness is maintained. Evening Arti was another attraction.

results.title: It’s ok
results.text: After reading reviews in TA we decided against entering the compound to avoid the 1000 rps fee which didn’t make sense, having just came from Patan Durbar square which also had 1000rps fee. Instead we walked around outside the temple and observed the local Hindus making their way in. The streets around the temple are a little charming, plenty character and selling worship items. We are obviously foreigners but never harassed and felt safe. There are signs everywhere that the zone outside the temple is a beggar free zone, in fact quite clean vs what we were expecting considering the reviews. We didn’t see any ceremony during the time we are there around midday.

results.title: Very Nice
results.text: Nice temple! according to our guide it is one of the oldest Hindu temple in Nepal. It is crematory place too.

results.title: Kathmandu.2019
results.text:
One of the power center of this earth.
Temple compound is well maintained and clean with all basic amenities. Step garden in well maintained, with a specific place for Pigeons to feed. We took a 1100.00NC receipt from NepalSBI within compound to worship Shiva from inside.

results.title: Major Hindu site
results.text: In a small location you get a lot. The main temple - that non-Hindus can't enter. The crematoria - where the dead are burned. Many small temples. Get a local guide - there's a lot to see.

results.title: Pasupatinath
results.text: Very good temple.Got darshan of evening Arti.it was excellent.Divine feeling in the middle of chanting prayers by a group of people.Done pradakshin inside the sanctum 2 times during arti . Very big compound.The cremation ghat near the temple is very dirty.No water in the river only a very little muddy water.

results.title: Must Visit Temple
results.text:
It is one of the beautiful temple I have visited, as soon as you enter the temple you see the Huge Nandi and the doorstep...The main shivalinga can be viewed from all the four sides, but once you are inside the sanctrum, you can see only 3 faces of Shivlinga, and for the fourth one you need to enter from the front. Main sanctrum has only natural lights which is very nice to preserve. Around the temple, you  will have small temple sof Bhairavnath and about 501 small shivalingas.

I found the temple interesting which had mix of Hindu and Chinese architecture (the adobe)
Avoid going on Saturday as it is rush day, and there is no system of queue (though is queue but it is largely mismanaged) on others days you could have peaceful darshan.

results.title: Impressing, interesting and a bit shocking
results.text: For the Pashupati and the crematorium we took a guide who was just at the entrance, where you pay the fee. Absolutely to recommend is Ananta! He told us a lot about the crematorium, the animal sacrifices and other Hindu traditons. As european for me it was fascinating but a bit shocking to see how the bodies were burned in public. But it's interesting to see how other cultures handle with the death. The temple cannot enter as a non-Hindu. So we could only see it from the outside.

results.title: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra 2019
results.text:
As part of the Kailash Yatra it is imperative to seek blessings from the Holy Pashupatinath temple, so we did get the blessings by way of evening aarti at the Temple.

As is common with every place which is thronged with too many people cleanliness is something which one has to be prepared to bear with.

Monkeys are also present in large numbers and one has to be careful with the belongings and eatables like Prasad etc.

This temple has historical significance and among the most important Jyotirling of Hindus. Situated on banks of Bagmati River in Kathmandu Nepal this is UNESCO designated cultural heritage site.

results.title: One of must visit Siva temple
results.text:
Thus temple complex is considered as the last one to be seen after the chardham darshan. With the huge crowd getting turned up here, it resembles a typical Indian temple.

The temple closes by noon ,hence plan the visit before 12.
A huge Nandi situated at entrance. The sanctum has four doors opening to four directions,revealing the four faces of the Linga. These all four doors will be open during abhisheka time.

In addition there temples of Vasuki, Lord Krishna, Ganapathi and Bhairava

No photography is allowed inside

Due to heavy rush, and poor queue arrangement , be alert on pick pocketers.

results.title: Impressive (‘holy’) place
results.text: I visited this place and a guide explained me about the meaning of it (be careful though because some of them ask quite some money). For me the most impressive part was to see how hindu’s deal with death. It is very different than in Western cultures because they burn the bodies near the river and throw the ash in it. It is a very normal thing here for the family to see the burning body. Children are swimming in the river as well (or looking for valuables?). Anyway: worth a visit and I would also recommend to ‘hire’ a guide to explain you about the place.
